_about: Edvard Grieg, In the Hall of the Mountain King (Peer Gynt, 1875; Grieg died 1907: public domain). Our own adaptation of the melody for the phase harp, written from the theme itself (no arrangement or transcription used). Read by tools/melody_curve.js; see notes/sea-song/README.md.
title: In the Hall of the Mountain King
_theme: [note, octave, eighths], 4/4: bars 1-4 as Grieg wrote them (B C# D E F# D F#, the answer E# C# E# / E C E, B C# D E F# D F# B, A F# D F# A), in the octave the piece sounds (B3 to B4). Round 2 plays every note as written: the piece has its own strings (the generator takes them from this list and codaChord).
_coda: crashing chords: [eighths after the previous, direction, the last B's octave]; each a rolled run of a whole turn ending on B, its chord notes (codaChord) sounding from the beat on, rising or falling with the roll (B3 D4 F#4 B4, then B4 F#4 D4 B3, then B3 D4 F#4 B4), the other lines silent; the first crash's first note is on the cut (the drum)
_F: F(z) = z^(n + i beta): the catalog's powa step. One statement is one clockwise turn; each statement is the one before scaled by e^(2 pi (1 + n turns) / beta) = e^(-pi/12) = 0.77 about 0, so constant speed plays it 1.30 times as fast (100, 130, 169, 219), and every turn lies inside the one before: the spiral never crosses itself (round 1's z^(-1+24i) with two turns a statement crossed itself 31 times).
_tempo: quarter = q0 at the start; the accelerando per statement is fixed by F (x1.30); from beat codaFrom (the first crash) the music broadens: each beat codaSlow times as long, so the coda's rolled chords stay within the speed the curve allows
_dynamics: main note velocity (from + (to - from)(b/48)^power), x downbeat on a bar's first beat, x long on notes of a quarter or more. Every crossing that is not a written note is silent (velocity 0). A crash's first note land, the rolled notes after it from roll[1] down to roll[0]. The drum: each cut tick at 20 log10(v / 0.9) + tickDb dB, v the written note it falls on, so it grows with the theme
_octave: each written note sounds on one string at its written pitch, its 2nd partial (the octave) at this level of the fundamental (-5 dB, for small speakers that lose the fundamental): one string a note, so the octave has one fixed level (round 2's second string at -10 dB added to the 2nd partial with a random phase: -20 to -2.6 dB, notes/sea-song/r2 review pitch-2)
_tuning: cents from equal temperament by pitch class, for every note of the piece: F# a just fifth (3:2) over B, so the final B-minor chord's fifth does not beat (B3's 3rd partial is F#4's 2nd exactly; review pitch-5); 2 cents, too small to hear in the melody. No other detune: a pitch is always the same string
_strings: the strings kept ringing at once: in the theme one (each note damps the one before as the next is plucked, over 30 ms, as a harpist damps a staccato line: no seconds ring together, review pitch-1), in the coda four (the chord B3 D4 F#4 B4); a string plucked again is damped first, as a harpist re-plucks it (review pitch-4)
_cutHandleR: the cut handle (and its angle label) inside the spiral's innermost turn instead of on the turns (review ui-4)
_pointsBy: the stored points are spread by arc length and by turning (half each), so the hairpins of the re-plucks are drawn with more points (review ui-2: no corner over about 12 degrees)

example._fit: the box kept in view (the curve spans x -1.60 to 1.26, y -1.39 to 1.62, and 0.12 to spare on each side); the plane's style bar is kept clear in pixels by the app (exFitTo: it does not scale with the view, review picture-2)

_cutDeg: the cut on the ray of bar 1's downbeat at 180 degrees: on z^(-2+24i) the GPU's float32 z^alpha needs |24 theta| < 88 on the branch, so the cut must be near 180 degrees
_turnPast: a turn of the melody goes this far (turns of arg F) past the last line it reaches, at most 42 % of the way to the next line (the harp's Schmitt band is 1/96 turn)
_crossSlope: arg F crosses a written note's line at least this fast (turns a beat): the Schmitt band is passed within 0.017 beat (10 ms at the start, 5 ms at the end)
_check: the generator's report 'look': the drawing at the phone's scale (128 px a unit): the most it turns within any 4 px of arc, its smallest radius over such an arc, and the narrowest gap between neighbouring turns, in px (review picture-3, picture-4)
